- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to dampen short-term spikes.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day lagged correction downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to ignore long-term trend; if sentiment is consistently positive, anchor forecast to 30-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits to recent noise; use 18-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
